scope: restricted serialized DIVDRA active runtime callsite composition

audit.note: Uses the existing single SWAP kernel and canonical serialized runtime; no use-case-specific kernel.
No files, parsers, formats, paths or file units enter kernel or runtime composition contracts.
Distribution parameters, explicit hydraulic views, scalar forcing, numerical config, committed state and results remain distinct typed categories.
No persistent drainage state is added; immutable distribution parameters and hydraulic views are referenced through compact registry indices.
Preflight probe and materialized drainage rows are transient composition scratch, never per-column persistent state.
Column-aligned requests and O(N) forcing-use counts avoid quadratic matching; no full forcing-registry copy is introduced.
Complete DIVDRA preflight precedes backend/checkpoint execution; accepted runs then use the unchanged checkpoint-trial-commit/rollback runtime.
External explicit view and scalar request can be cheaply replayed; no hidden mutation of committed physical state is used as a start condition.
Composition accepts generic t0,t1 and introduces no day/month/year boundary.
No coupling-window duration assumption is introduced.
Existing transactional runtime remains compatible with future coupling composition; F-MR34 adds no competing coupling path.
No groundwater-interface head/flux contract is altered; the supplied groundwater level is only part of the explicit hydraulic view.
Scalar soil-to-drain transfer remains authoritative; node distribution enters the existing source/sink ledger exactly once and no second mass booking is added.
No interface sensitivity is hidden or approximated; response tangents remain explicitly out of scope.
One process projection plus one ordinary runtime execution is used; no multi-run coupling pattern is introduced.
Feature-active memory scales with active requested rows; generic serialized runtime remains byte-identical and MultiSWAP batching is preserved.
No MODFLOW-cell, tile or area-fraction relation enters the composition.
No deep-vadose transfer behavior is introduced or assumed.
No component-transition storage or transfer bookkeeping is changed.
DIVDRA consumes process_hydraulic_view_t and is not coupled to a particular Richards implementation.
Existing drainage process and existing source/sink physics are reused; legacy globals are not used by production code.
Production composition imports no HeadCalc internals and consumes only the public hydraulic-view/process contracts.
No solver-policy option is added and no physical option is silently changed by numerical policy.
Preflight is bounded O(N) and fail-closed; no unbounded retry or fallback path is introduced.
Reference runtime remains unchanged and available; F-MR34 is qualified against the canonical reference execution path.
Sparse per-active-column composition/binding diagnostics expose status, forcing handle and process diagnostics.
When this optional route is not called there is zero F-MR34 allocation; within the route only active requests materialize drainage rows.
System composition remains in runtime; SWAP process code knows nothing about external system layout.
No midnight, one-day, .swp, path or direct MODFLOW assumption is introduced.
This artifact explicitly records the assessment of all 30 architecture invariants before qualification.
